title: Candy
author: Mian Mian
current_text: Chinese authorities banned Mian Mian’s Candy in China in 2000, denouncing her as “a poster child for spiritual pollution”; the book subsequently became an underground hit.

sources.quote: Chinese authorities banned Mian Mian's first novel, Candy, when it was published in 2000, denouncing her as "a poster child for spiritual pollution."
sources.title: FRONTLINE/WORLD . CHINA - Shanghai Nights . Notorious Writer, Forbidden StoriesRead excerpts from Candy | PBS

sources.quote: Censors outlawed the publication of Mian Mian's breakthrough novel Candy - a depiction of sex and drugs amongst the youth of two major cities - five years ago, although this did not prevent it becoming an underground hit.
sources.title: BBC NEWS | Entertainment | Author Mian Mian challenges China

sources.quote: Ever since Mian Mian's Candy and literary counterpart Zhou Weihui's Shanghai Baby -- both banned books in China -- a growing circle of local and foreign artists and cultural experts have chronicled the city's vibrant underground life.
sources.title: Shanghai emerges from `Maoist straitjacket' - Taipei Times

ban_rows.note: Withdrawn from sale in mainland China shortly after publication and denounced by the Chinese press as "spiritual pollution"; the official campaign also targeted Wei Hui's Shanghai Baby. Both novels remained out of print on the mainland for over a decade.
